items.title: Holly Hofmann interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: That came about through another wonderful jazz musician named Slide Hampton, who heard me at a Jamey Aebersold clinic when I was in college, and we struck up a friendship and a long — years later we still get a chance to play together upon occasion.

ctx.x: I see Frank Wess show up on your list of people that you’ve played with and studied with? How did that come about?

That came about through another wonderful jazz musician named Slide Hampton, who heard me at a Jamey Aebersold clinic when I was in college, and we struck up a friendship and a long — years later we still get a chance to play together upon occasion. And he suggested that I come to New York during the summers and study with Frank a bit, which I did several different summers in college. And that was a wonderful experience. And Frank, to this day, in fact we’re going to be playing together on the West Coast Jazz…
Yeah. There seems to be a — let’s say historical confusion about who actually was the first, or at least flute player to appear on a jazz record. Some say it was Frank, I’ve heard Sam Most.
